Coverage flag: the full local 2018 file contains 739 records of all types, while BC reports 2,117 fires. This gap exists before any seasonal/date filters. Published totals and the incident layer may differ in definition or revision; this file is not a verified complete census. BC annual totals use an April-March reporting period. Calendar-year mismatch is excluded here, not automatically classified as bad data.

FIRMS: presumed vegetation thermal detections (type 0). BC: Fire records with usable year-consistent dates. Missing records are not verified fire absence.

Proximity is not a verified event match: another fire can supply the nearby detection. All sensitivity windows use the same May 4-August 31 cohort, with observations available through September 30. Endpoints are inclusive. Recorded size is retrospective, used only for diagnosis. No nearby detection does not prove a false incident or a satellite miss.

Nodes are positive H3 cell-days. Links join the same or adjacent cells across up to 1, 3 or 7 days. Connected chains can merge separate fires or split one fire. These are retrospective diagnostic groups, not ignition labels or confirmed incidents.

Interpretation and next label work

  • Compare occupied-cell maps before interpreting raw detection intensity as spatial coverage.
  • Audit dates, record types and observation availability before treating BC and FIRMS disagreements as label errors.
  • Use official perimeters and incident IDs to validate event grouping; retain ambiguous matches.
  • Keep recorded new starts and ongoing hotspot activity as separate targets. Never infer daily burn extent from a final perimeter.

Sources: NASA FIRMS fields; NASA detection limitations; BC historical incidents.
